Theme

Latin word

rēctus

rēctus, rēcta, rēctum

declension

right, correct; straight, direct; right, sound (of advice, a judgement); regular, formal (of a dinner)

In this lexicon

  • correct

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Ac. 1.19: quid vērum, quid falsum, quid rēctum in ōrātiōne prāvumve; Traupman 28, 246; Traupman 297

  • direct

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Eun. 87: cūr nōn rēctā intrōībās?; Traupman 213: volāre rēctā in Austriam, to fly directly to Austria; Traupman 203, 304: directly, rēctā, per dīrēctum; Traupman 204: in a straight line, per dīrēctum

  • good

    also used · classical · Traupman 322

  • proper

    also used · classical · Suet. Dom. 7: rēctārum cēnārum cōnsuētūdō (Lewis & Short, s.v. regō); Mart. 2.69.7

  • rēctus cāsus: nominative

    classical

Notes

  1. 1A participle in -tus from a root ending in g has a long vowel: āctus, lēctus, rēctus, tēctus, tāctus, frāctus, and pāctus from pangō. Their derivatives keep it: āctiō, lēctiō, tēctum, dēlēctus, frāctūra. Ruling: Lachmann’s law: āctus, lēctus, frāctus.
